fix.digest: Working on Galileo's scrambled letters, Kepler produces a Latin line that he takes to greet the twin offspring of Mars, which fitted his own guess that Mars should have two moons. He later prints his attempt. He is wrong about the message, though Mars does have two small moons, found in 1877.

problem: The quote is a modernised paraphrase; the letter as printed from the manuscript reads roughly 'like a tarte that my cooke made me the last weeke'. A quote should follow the printed original's words. [Editor: quote dropped; wording not checked against the printed letter.]
The comparison of a lunar cavity to Bohemia comes from the text of Sidereus Nuncius (1610), not from the watercolours themselves.

fix.digest: With a new glass of about twenty power, Galileo paints a series of washes of the Moon at different phases, showing the terminator broken by bright points that he reads as mountain-tops catching the dawn, and dark hollows; in the printed book he will compare one great hollow to Bohemia ringed by mountains. The dating is reconstructed: E. Whitaker put them between 30 November and 18 December 1609, while others argue some belong to November. These drawings become the engravings in Sidereus Nuncius.

problem: The explicit statement that the Venus observation favours the Copernican/Pythagorean system is clearest in Galileo's letters around the 1 January 1611 solution and his 30 December 1610 letters; the 11 December letter announced the cipher of a new, important observation.

fix.digest: Galileo sends Giuliano another scrambled Latin line, announcing only that he has made a new observation of great consequence, without saying what it is. He has been watching Venus shrink and change from round toward half and crescent over the autumn. This is the observation that most directly contradicts a Ptolemaic arrangement, as his letters of the following weeks make plain.

problem: Caption already states plainly it is a forgery (good). It can name the probable forger so no reader mistakes the leaf for Galileo's hand.

fix.caption: Long displayed as Galileo's draft to the Doge with his first Jupiter notes, this leaf is a forgery: in 2022 the University of Michigan confirmed it was made in the twentieth century, probably by the forger Tobia Nicotra. It is not Galileo's hand; the authentic letter is in the Venetian state archives.

problem: Two problems. (1) 30 March 1754 corresponds only to the intercalary 2nd month, 7th day (that month began c. 24 March 1754; the ordinary 2nd month's 7th day was c. 28 February), so the display should not hedge. (2) Yamawaki did not find a mismatch with the 'nine viscera': he took what he saw to agree with the ancient 'nine viscera' (九蔵) of the Zhouli rather than the later orthodox scheme of five viscera and six bowels.

fix.digest: After a petition he made with the Obama-domain physician Kosugi Genteki, Yamawaki is allowed to watch the opening of a man executed in Kyoto. The man was one of five beheaded, the one whose burial was delayed. Yamawaki studies the organs of the chest and abdomen and judges that they fit the ancient 'nine viscera' of the Zhou li better than the later orthodox scheme of five viscera and six bowels. Because there is no head, there is nothing to record about the brain.

fix.digest: Nakagawa writes in Dutch, addressing the letter to Hoffman in Batavia to be passed on to Thunberg. He thanks Thunberg for his teaching in herbal medicine and pharmacy, sends about a hundred kinds of seeds and dried plants through an interpreter, and asks for two large dictionaries, which he attributes to Pieter Marin. Six years after Kotsugahara, the lack of a proper dictionary is still the group's main problem.

fix.digest: A year after the Origin, Wallace told Bates that he could not fully express his admiration for Darwin's book, that he could never have approached its completeness, evidence and argument, and that Darwin had created a new science and a new philosophy.
